It is modeled as a negative exponential function, where the rate of decay reflects physiological constraints on temporal processing. The optimal phase occurs when the conditioned stimulus precedes the unconditioned stimulus by approximately 0.44 seconds, aligning with prior experimental findings. This principle underpins both Bayesian inference in GSI—where temporal alignment informs conditional probabilities—and state-transition logic in GSE, where optimal timing enables efficient policy updates. The negative growth function fitting provides empirical validation, showing near-perfect correlation between theoretical predictions and observed data points. The gradient’s continuity implies that backward conditioning is not a distinct phenomenon but an extreme case of a continuous temporal efficiency spectrum.
